doc: Per-type physical defaults for the tier-1 physics layer (docs/design/TIER1_PHYSICS.md 4.6; read through props). A row holds record field names (TIER1_PHYSICS 4.8) used as defaults between the entity record (which always wins) and the material class. Rows match the record's type, then its is_a chain (nearest first), then the head noun of the type name (the last word: wine_bottle -> bottle), then its category, then its tags; for each field the most specific row that sets it wins. `material` in a row is used only when the type chain declares no material. Ratings are in kg and are scaled by the per-instance variation (props.vary) unless the entity sets phys_exact.

fields.rating_kg: load a surface (or a non-shelved container) carries before it fails
fields.shelf_rating_kg: load one shelf of shelved furniture carries
fields.hang_kg: load hung on a hook, rail or rod; {"per_m": kg} scales with the rod length (size_m[0]), {"per_slot": kg} with the record's hang_slots (a rail of hooks)
fields.handle_kg: contents a carried container's handles or bottom hold
fields.rim_m: how deep liquid can pool on it before running off
fields.mouth_frac: mouth width as a fraction of the inner width (narrow neck < 0.6)
fields.shape: box, cylinder, sphere, flat or long (rolling and choking checks)
fields.com_frac: height of the centre of mass as a fraction of the height
fields.tempered: glass in it is tempered (class tempered_glass)
fields.hard: impact hardness as a landing surface (beds and sofas are soft landings)
fields.cushion_m / cushion_j: a soft landing's cushion (floors.json columns of the same names): the depth that stops a falling item and the energy it takes before it bottoms out
fields.base_m: width of the foot an upright item stands on, when narrower than its bounding box (stemware, lamps): the tip threshold uses it
fields.drag_cd: wind drag coefficient over the item's outline; rows only lower it below the bluff-body 1.2 (open frames such as chairs and racks)
fields.nest_group / nest_frac: items of one nest group stack inside each other: after the first, each counts nest_frac of its volume
fields.floats: whether the item floats in fresh water, when its material alone would say otherwise (buoyancy aids, fruit with air in its tissue)
fields.airtight: a sealed hollow item (an inflatable): it floats when its mass is less than the water its outline displaces

bookshelf.source: particleboard bookcase shelf: about 25-30 kg before it bows (admin_inventory SHELF_RATING 25)

shelf_unit.source: boltless steel or wire shelving: about 90-150 kg per shelf (admin_inventory 90)

closet_shelving.source: closet wire or melamine shelf on standards: about 25 kg

cabinet.source: base-cabinet shelf (0.75 x 0.55 m): ANSI/KCMA A161.1 shelf load test 15 lb/ft2 = about 30 kg

upper_cabinet.source: upper-cabinet shelf (0.75 x 0.3 m): KCMA 15 lb/ft2 = about 18 kg, 20 kg used (the spec corrects admin's 15)

filing_cabinet.source: full-extension filing drawer: about 30-45 kg (letter-size steel cabinets)

wardrobe.source: wardrobe or closet shelf: about 40 kg

closet.source: wardrobe or closet shelf: about 40 kg

wall_shelf.source: floating wall shelf on a concealed bracket: about 10-15 kg (admin_inventory SURFACE_RATING 12)

table.source: light four-leg kitchen table: about 50 kg distributed

side_table.source: side or end table: about 20 kg

tv_stand.source: TV stand or media console: about 45 kg

counter.source: kitchen counter on base cabinets: about 200 kg

chair.source: chair seat: BIFMA X5.1 functional seat load 250 lb = 113 kg; an open frame (legs, seat, slatted back) catches wind like Cd 0.7 over its outline (about half solid, member Cd 1.2-2): a 3-4 kg chair slides at about 9 m/s (TIER1_PHYSICS 12.4 anchor)

sofa.source: three-seat sofa: 3 x 113 kg; a soft landing (0.15); only the cushions and cover soak up liquid (about 0.3 L per kg of the whole piece)

armchair.source: upholstered seat: a soft landing (0.15); cushions and cover hold about 0.3 L per kg of the whole piece

bed.source: bed frame with mattress: about 250 kg and up; a mattress is a soft landing (0.15): 15 cm of springs and foam take a person's fall

pet_bed.source: cushioned pet bed: a soft landing (about 6 cm of fill)

window_sill.source: interior window sill board: about 10 kg

climbing_aid.source: ANSI A14.2 type III step stool: 200 lb = about 90 kg (an explicit rated_kg on the type wins)

closet_rod.source: closet rod on brackets: about 25 kg per metre of loaded rod

laundry_basket.source: plastic laundry basket handles: about 15 kg

box.source: medium single-wall cardboard box: the taped bottom gives way above about 15 kg

baking_sheet.source: rimmed half-sheet pan: about 2 cm rim

bathtub.source: alcove bathtub: about 0.38-0.4 m interior depth (the type's inner_size_m height 0.4; the spec's 0.5 is the outer height)

rolling_pin.source: a rolling pin is a cylinder

floor_lamp.source: floor lamp with a weighted base about 30 cm across under a wider shade

table_lamp.source: table lamp: heavy base about 20 cm across, light wider shade: it tips at about 0.2 / (2 x 0.21) = 0.48 g (TIER1_PHYSICS 5.4: about 0.5 g)

wine_glass.source: stemware: a thin bowl on a tall stem standing on a 7 cm foot, centre of mass about 11 cm up a 20 cm glass: it tips at 0.07 / (2 x 0.11) = 0.32 g (TIER1_PHYSICS 5.4) and breaks from about 0.25 m onto tile (4.3); still soda-lime glass for heat

patio_umbrella.source: patio umbrella as installed in its weighted base

pedestal_fan.source: pedestal fan: the motor head sits on a tall pole

baby_bottle.source: baby bottles have wide necks for filling and cleaning: about 4 cm on a 5 cm inside (standard necks 3.5 cm, wide necks 5 cm), not the 0.3 of the bottle noun

blender_jar.source: a blender jar opens over its whole top (the lid covers it all), not the 0.8 of the jar noun

casserole_dish.source: glass bakeware (Pyrex, Anchor Hocking) is tempered soda-lime made for oven heat: a room-temperature dish into a 220 C oven (about 200 K x 0.5) does not crack

liquid_measuring_cup.source: glass measuring jugs are tempered for boiling liquids and the microwave

french_press.source: a French press beaker is borosilicate 3.3 made for boiling water (about 160 K); it still breaks from a drop like other thin glass

mason_jar.source: canning jars are heat-treated soda-lime made for boiling-water canning (about 60 K against 45 K for annealed jars); makers still ask for warm jars before hot fills, so boiling soup into a fridge-cold jar can crack it

sliding_door.source: glass in doors must be safety glazing (IRC R308.4.1)

french_door.source: glass in doors must be safety glazing (IRC R308.4.1)

laptop_computer.source: laptops survive about desk height (0.75 m) onto a hard floor (MIL-STD-810 rugged models 1.2 m; consumer about 0.75-1 m); nominal 0.9 m so every instance of the +-15 % band (0.77-1.04 m) survives the desk-height anchor

paper_towel_roll.source: paper towel holds 5-8 g of water per g

waste_container.source: household bins are mostly rectangular (overrides the noun 'can' of trash_can)

hair_dryer.source: hair dryer: plastic shell, heater and motor

scanner_glass.source: a flat scanner platen (overrides the noun glass)

watering_can.source: a watering can does not roll (overrides the noun can)

key_hook.source: a key rack's small cup hooks: about 1-3 kg each

garden_tool_rack.source: a wall-mounted garage tool rack: about 10 kg per slot (heavy-duty racks list 15-50 lb per hook): 10 slots of rakes, spades and a wheel hose carry 100 kg

sand_bag.source: a sandbag's mass is sand (porosity 35-40 % at a bulk 1.5-1.7 t/m3: about 0.25 L of water per kg) in a canvas or woven polypropylene sack; counting the 10 kg as canvas gave 25 L in a 10 L bag

foam_play_mat.source: interlocking play mats are EVA closed-cell foam: wipe-clean, they take up next to no water and float

foam_roller.source: foam rollers are closed-cell EPP, EPE or EVA foam

pool_float.source: an inflated PVC lounger: sealed air chambers

bottle.source: bottles: round, narrow neck (wine bottle bore 18.5 mm on a 75 mm body); a full bottle's COM sits a little below mid-height

jug.source: jugs: narrow neck (a gallon milk jug's 38 mm cap on a 150 mm body)

jar.source: jars: wide mouth (a regular-mouth mason jar's 60 mm opening on a 75 mm body)

cup.source: cups nest: each extra cup adds about 40 % of its volume

bowl.source: bowls nest: each extra bowl adds about 30 % of its volume

vase.source: vases: round, mouth about 60 % of the body

orange.source: citrus is round; the peel's air makes it float (about 0.85-0.95 g/cm3)

apple.source: apples are round and float: about a quarter of their volume is air (0.75-0.85 g/cm3)

onion.source: onions are round and float (air between the layers)

grapefruit.source: citrus is round; the peel's air makes it float (about 0.85-0.95 g/cm3)

lemon.source: citrus is round; the peel's air makes it float (about 0.85-0.95 g/cm3)

lime.source: citrus is round; the peel's air makes it float (about 0.85-0.95 g/cm3)

egg.source: a hen's egg: a rigid shell that cracks from a few centimetres; it rolls (in arcs)

tray.source: serving trays: flat with a 2 cm lip

rod.source: curtain rod on two brackets: about 8 kg

rack.source: racks (drying, shoe, firewood, tool) are open frames: Cd about 0.7 over their outline

trivet.source: trivets carry pans straight from the oven

pillow.source: a pillow is a soft landing (about 10 cm of fill)

mattress.source: a mattress is a soft landing (15 cm of springs and foam)

cushion.source: a cushion is a soft landing (about 6 cm of foam)
cushions are soft landings (about 6 cm of foam)

hooks.source: a hook, or a rail or rack of them screwed into studs or with proper anchors: each hook about 5-10 kg (robe and coat hooks are sold for 10-25 lb) and the rail carries the sum: a 6-hook coat rail about 42 kg, not one hook's 10 kg for the whole rail

sink.source: sink basin: about 0.2 m deep to the overflow

tv.source: flat-panel TVs crack their panel from a low tip or drop (about 0.3 m)

flotation.source: ring buoys and life jackets are closed-cell PE or PVC foam in a cover (USCG-approved devices must not take up water): they soak up next to nothing and float

phone.source: smartphones are drop-rated to about 1 m: nominal 1.2 m so every instance of the +-15 % band (1.02-1.38 m) survives a 1 m drop onto tile (TIER1_PHYSICS 4.3)

glass_top.source: glass-top table: tempered glass, about 25 kg

fillers.doc: Deterministic filler items for the `load` setup op (TIER1_PHYSICS 7.5): the first listed type that the registry knows, else generic_item; `props` are always applied so the mass is exact.

boxes.source: a filled storage box: about 3 kg

towels.source: a folded bath towel: about 0.5 kg

people.doc: Helper capacities for team lifts and pushes (forces.lift_plan, forces.max_push_n). A person's own lift_kg (or manipulation's max_lift_kg) and push_n win; anyone whose abilities.mobility is not "full" counts 0.

adult.source: revised NIOSH lifting equation load constant 23 kg (51 lb); sustained two-hand push about 200 N (Snook and Ciriello tables)

teen.source: adolescent lifting guidance about two thirds of the adult constant

elderly.source: older adults: reduced strength, fall risk

child.source: the robot never enlists a child for a heavy lift
